main_text.p: riarum in disputatione de cœna Domini confundantur, cùm realiter & substantialiter iuncta putantur & dicuntur, quæ nō nisi relatiuorum more, tanquam signa cum rebus suis significatis, coniunguntur. Qua de re mox plura, Deo volente, dicemus.

Alter paralogismus rerum in negotio cœnæ frequentissimus, est, Τοῦ ἐ-λέγχ[?] ἄγνοια. Huc pertinent longæ declamationes de omnipotentia Dei, de coniunctione duarum naturarum in Christo, de sessione ad dexteram Dei: quæ omnia planè sunt ἀπερ[?]σδιό-νυστα[?], quantùm ad propositam quæstionem attinet: multò etiam magis, encomia illa de maiestate, veritate & constantia verbi Dei: item, quæ de imbecillitate peruersitatéque humanæ sapientiæ, rationis, sensuum, in rebus diuinis, ad pauorem panicum iniiciẽdum, haud aliter aggregantur & exaggeratur, quàm Mithridaticum bellum & Cannẽsis pugna adscisceban-tur ab aduocato in leuissima causa, ut est

page.notes: The Greek phrase "Τοῦ ἐ-λέγχ[?] ἄγνοια" and the Greek word "ἀπερ[?]σδιό-νυστα[?]" are uncertain at the line ends; the letters are only partly legible. The word "iniiciẽdum" keeps the printed tilde over e as an abbreviation for n. Long s and the printed f forms are rendered as plain s throughout. The right-hand margin has only faint marks from the adjoining page and show-through, which are not transcribed.
